question_text: If the tangent at any point on the curve x²⁄³ + y²⁄³ = a²⁄³ intersects the coordinate axes in A and B, show that the length AB is a constant.

steps.margin_note: First mark. The question says at ANY point, so the point must be general. The parametric form removes the two-thirds powers before any differentiation starts, which is why it is written first even though the question never mentions θ.

steps.why: Raising a cos³θ to the power 2/3 leaves cos²θ, so the awkward index disappears in one line. Working with x and y directly needs implicit differentiation with x⁻¹⁄³ terms, which is longer and harder to keep clean.
common_mistakes: Taking a numbered point with fixed values, which proves nothing about ANY point.
Writing the point as (a cos²θ, a sin²θ), which does not satisfy the curve.
Skipping the check that P lies on the curve.
steps.memory_tip: The power on the curve is 2/3, so the power inside the point is 3 — the cube inside times the two-thirds outside gives the power 2.

steps.label: Find the slope of the tangent
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Differentiate x and y separately with respect to θ, then divide. The factor 3a cancels, so the slope depends only on θ.

steps.why: For a curve given by a parameter, dy/dx is the ratio of the two θ-derivatives. Writing dy/dθ alone and calling it the slope is a common error at this line.
common_mistakes: Dividing dx/dθ by dy/dθ, which gives the reciprocal of the slope.
Losing the minus sign that comes from differentiating cos³θ.
Calling dy/dθ the slope of the tangent.
steps.memory_tip: Top over bottom, both with respect to θ: dy/dθ goes above, dx/dθ goes below.

steps.margin_note: Third mark. Reduce the tangent to intercept form x/p + y/q = 1, where p and q are the intercepts. Once it is in that form the two intercepts are read straight off with no further working.

steps.why: The identity cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 reduces the right side to a sinθ cosθ in one line, and dividing by it gives the intercept form directly. Putting y = 0 and x = 0 into the unsimplified tangent gives the same two intercepts in a different way.
common_mistakes: Not multiplying both sides by cosθ, so tanθ stays in the equation and it does not reach the intercept form.
Reading the intercepts as a sinθ and a cosθ, with the two swapped.
Dividing by a sinθ cosθ but leaving the right side as something other than 1.
steps.memory_tip: Intercept form is x/p + y/q = 1, so the number under x is the x-intercept and the number under y is the y-intercept.
lines_compact: Tangent at P:  y − a sin³θ = −tanθ (x − a cos³θ)
y cosθ − a sin³θ cosθ = −x sinθ + a sinθ cos³θ
x sinθ + y cosθ = a sinθ cos³θ + a sin³θ cosθ
= a sinθ cosθ (cos²θ + sin²θ) = a sinθ cosθ
This is the intercept form, so the tangent meets the axes at
A = (a cosθ, 0)   and   B = (0, a sinθ)

steps.label: Find AB and show it is free of θ
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The examiner is looking for θ to disappear. Stopping at √(a²cos²θ + a²sin²θ) does not answer the question, because the question asks for a constant.

lines.text: the length AB is the same at every point
of the curve, so it is a constant.

recall.must_convey: That AB = |a| because cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 removes θ, so the length is constant.

steps.why: A constant means free of the parameter. The identity cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 is what removes θ, and saying so is the sentence that finishes the proof.
common_mistakes: Writing √(a²) as a and losing the modulus when a could be negative.
Leaving the answer as √(a²cos²θ + a²sin²θ) and calling it constant without simplifying.
Using the distance formula between P and A instead of between A and B.
steps.memory_tip: A sits on the x-axis and B sits on the y-axis, so AB is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs a cosθ and a sinθ — and that hypotenuse is |a|.

lines_compact.text: the length AB is the same at every point
of the curve, so it is a constant.

insider_note: Use the parametric point (a cos³θ, a sin³θ) — the implicit form makes the intercepts far messier. AB then comes out as |a|, free of θ, which proves the claim.
